title: Find the integrating factor
text: Put the equation in the form $$y'+p\left(x\right) y=q(x)$$, then multiply by the integrating factor so the left side becomes the derivative of the integrating factor times $$y$$.

title: Integrate and solve
text: Dividing by $$x^2$$ gives $$y'-\frac{y}{x}=\frac{-\ln\left(x\right)}{x^2}$$. With integrating factor $$\frac{1}{x}$$, the derivative of $$\frac{y}{x}$$ is $$\frac{-\ln\left(x\right)}{x^3}$$. Integrating by parts gives $$\frac{y}{x}=\frac{\ln\left(x\right)}{2x^2}+\frac{1}{4x^2}+C$$. $$y(1)=1$$ gives $$C=\frac{3}{4}$$, so $$y=\frac{\ln\left(x\right)}{2x}+\frac{1}{4x}+\frac{3x}{4}$$.
